title: Exchange rates cached forever: pricing uses rates that never expire
business_context: BureauX charges international customers in local currency using exchange rates pulled from a rates provider. The provider updates rates several times a day; the finance contract is that a rate older than 10 minutes must never be used for pricing — otherwise the margin between the quoted rate and the settlement rate is lost.
user_request: Finance noticed that when the rates provider updates mid-day, our quoted prices keep using the morning rates until the next deploy. The rates service caches its responses — someone made them permanent. Pricing must refresh from the provider at most 10 minutes after the last fetch, while still shielding the provider from a request-per-quote. The rates service interface stays the same.

intentional_defect.summary: The rates service uses Cache::rememberForever('rates:USD:EUR', ...): the cached rate never expires, so pricing uses the first-fetched rate until the cache is manually flushed.
intentional_defect.root_cause: rememberForever stores without a TTL. The provider contract says rates older than 10 minutes are unquotable, but nothing in the cache layer enforces that window.
intentional_defect.why_it_looks_correct: rememberForever is a documented Cache method, the fallback closure is correct, and every test sees a working rate — the staleness only appears across TIME, which no test travels through.

non_obvious_invariant: A cached rate older than 10 minutes must be re-fetched from the provider; a rate fetched within the last 10 minutes must be served from the cache without hitting the provider again.
expected_diagnosis: The agent must recognize that rememberForever violates the 10-minute freshness window and switch to a TTL'd cache entry (Cache::remember with a 10-minute expiry).
safe_fix_constraints: The rates service interface stays unchanged.
The freshness window is 10 minutes: older rates must be re-fetched, fresher ones served from cache.
failure_explanation: Pricing is computed from morning rates all day long: every international sale between the provider's updates and the next deploy loses the margin between the quoted and the settled rate — on high-volume days that is a direct, compounding revenue leak that no test or log surfaces because the cache is working 'as written'.
